advertising-policies-202604.headline: Adds verification checks for suspicious advertisers and financial ads
advertising-policies-202604.summary: Meta may now require extra verification from advertisers that show "potentially suspicious behavior" or run ads in categories likely to be targeted by scammers, and says ad accounts "must be associated with a legitimate business or individual". Financial services advertisers, who before had to show they were authorised by regulators, now "may be required to" verify their identity and show that authorisation.

advertising-policies-202607.headline: Renames weight loss ad rules and removes body-image wording
advertising-policies-202607.summary: The "Weight Loss and Cosmetic Products and Procedures" category becomes "Health and Wellbeing", and the rule that such ads target only people aged 18 or over now also covers weight gain products. Meta removed the sentence barring ads that imply "negative self-perception" or a "perfect body type", and added that ads must not contain "certain claims prohibited by our policy".

advertising-policies-202610.headline: Renames scam ad rules and adds a fake documents section
advertising-policies-202610.summary: The "Fraud, Scams and Deceptive Practices" section becomes "Prohibited Commercial Practices", pointing to the Community Standard of that name, and loses its sentence on deceptive offers and the April line on extra checks for suspicious advertisers. A new section bars ads promoting trade in fake, forged or stolen documents, manipulated devices or subscriptions, personal information, cheating products, money muling and money laundering.

advertising-policies-202611.headline: Requires financial services advertisers to verify their identity
advertising-policies-202611.summary: Advertisers promoting financial products and services now "are required" to verify their business or individual identity and show they are authorised by regulators where this is a requirement. Until now the standards said they "may be required" to do so, wording Meta added in April 2026.

ai-terms-202412.headline: Adds separate AI terms for the UK, Brazil and the EU
ai-terms-202412.summary: The terms now say users in the United Kingdom, Brazil and the "European Region" each have their own Meta AIs Terms of Service for Meta's generative AI products and features. This replaces a note that only pointed UK users to separate UK terms.

ai-terms-202502.headline: Clarifies warning on sharing sensitive information and updates date
ai-terms-202502.summary: Meta added "such as" to the warning not to share information users don't want the AIs to use and retain, so account identifiers, passwords and financial information now read as examples of sensitive information. The "Last Updated" date moves from 8 October 2024 to 17 January 2025.

ai-terms-202506.headline: Adds Private Processing promise and drops effective and update dates
ai-terms-202506.summary: Meta added that when users share private messages with friends and family for AI features that use "Private Processing technology", Meta "cannot read or access" them, and that it provides Private Processing as a service on users' behalf. The effective date (23 July 2024) and last updated date (17 January 2025) no longer appear at the end of the page.

ai-terms-202507.headline: Adds psychological advice ban and a professional care disclaimer
ai-terms-202507.summary: Meta added "psychological" to the medical, financial and legal advice that users may not solicit from its AIs. It also added that nothing the AIs generate "should be interpreted as an offer or provision of professional care" or as a substitute for a qualified provider.

ai-terms-202601.headline: Rewrites AI terms with new banned uses and media consent rules
ai-terms-202601.summary: A broad rewrite, effective 18 December 2025. Meta bans more uses, including classifying people by social behaviour, predictive policing, scraping faces for recognition databases and workplace emotion recognition, and says it uses AI interactions to "personalize your experiences and ads". A section on analysing faces in images, with its Illinois and Texas rule, becomes "Media Processing", where users must confirm they have consent from the people shown.

ai-terms-202605.headline: Menu or layout change only
ai-terms-202605.summary: A second "Effective" label appears beside the effective date, which stays at 18 December 2025, and the terms' wording did not change.

ai-terms-202606.headline: Widens Private Processing wording and adds search partner detail
ai-terms-202606.summary: Meta reworded its Private Processing promise: it "cannot read or access" messages in any "AI chats that use Private Processing technology", not only messages shared with friends and family. It added that search terms based on such chats may go to search partners, but "These queries are not connected to your account." The effective date moves to 13 May 2026.

audience-network-policy-202607.headline: Adds an "Updated" date of 20 April 2026
audience-network-policy-202607.summary: The page now shows "Updated: Apr 20, 2026" at the top, and the wording of the policy did not change.

audience-network-policy-202610.headline: Menu or layout change only
audience-network-policy-202610.summary: The policy rules now appear as a bulleted list, with the wording of each rule unchanged.

avatar-terms-202508.headline: Menu or layout change only
avatar-terms-202508.summary: The site menus, footer, a marketing sign-up box and Meta Quest and Ray-Ban Meta product notices no longer appear on the page, and the avatar terms' wording did not change.

avatar-terms-202602.headline: Removes the Avatars Store and its purchase and refund terms
avatar-terms-202602.summary: Meta removed the Avatars Store section and its rules on purchases, payment data, taxes and refunds, including the line that all acquisitions are final. Users now "acquire" licensed avatar items, and the Meta Horizon Digital Items Terms and Meta Credits Terms now also apply. Lines denying refunds for items lost when an account is suspended, deleted or converted to a business account are also gone.

brand-resources-202502.headline: Removes the list of uses that need Meta's permission
brand-resources-202502.summary: Meta removed the line asking people to "submit a request for permission" before using its brand assets, and the list of uses it covered: marketing or advertising on TV or online; books, plays, TV shows and film scripts; print packaging; and partnership activations and branding. The "Submit your request" and "My requests" links also went. The list did not come back in later copies.

brand-resources-202512.headline: Menu or layout change only
brand-resources-202512.summary: A "My Requests" link returned to the page; the wording did not change.

branded-content-policies-202504.headline: Menu or layout change only
branded-content-policies-202504.summary: A "Learn more" link changes from "Get Approval From Your Business Partners" to "Tag a Business Partner in a Branded Content Post", and the policy wording is unchanged.

branded-content-policies-202509.headline: Drops note that the branded content tool is limited to some regions
branded-content-policies-202509.summary: Meta removed the line saying the branded content tool "is only available to certain Pages in certain regions at this time". It also renamed and trimmed the "Learn more" links, dropping those for Brand Collabs Manager and "Get Discovered by Advertisers".

commerce-policies-202502.headline: Defines commerce content and widens bans to Messenger and piracy tools
commerce-policies-202502.summary: Meta added a definition of commerce content as any attempt to buy, sell or trade products, "even for free", on its commerce services such as Marketplace, Shops and WhatsApp Business Catalog. The anti-discrimination rule now also covers "commerce Messenger threads". The ban on unauthorised copies now covers services or devices that help distribute them, and names TV shows, broadcasts, books and images.

commerce-policies-202504.headline: Limits business selling on Marketplace in the EEA, Philippines and India
commerce-policies-202504.summary: The policies now say Facebook Marketplace "is intended for consumer-to-consumer sales". Businesses, and individuals acting in a business capacity, in the European Economic Area, the Philippines and India may lose access to Marketplace or have their listings removed if they try to sell there.

commercial-terms-202502.headline: Menu or layout change only
commercial-terms-202502.summary: The disputes section now appears as a bulleted list, and the arbitration and US courts wording is unchanged.

commercial-terms-202505.headline: Menu or layout change only
commercial-terms-202505.summary: The disputes section returns from a bulleted list to running text, and the arbitration and US courts wording is unchanged.

commercial-terms-202610.headline: Announces updated Commercial Terms taking effect on 20 November 2026
commercial-terms-202610.summary: Meta added a notice that it is updating the Commercial Terms, with the changes due to take effect on 20 November 2026, and a link to read them. Meta's address in the terms changes from 1601 Willow Rd. to 1 Meta Way, Menlo Park.

commercial-terms-202611.headline: Puts the planned Commercial Terms update on hold
commercial-terms-202611.summary: Meta now says the updated Commercial Terms, which had been due to take effect on 20 November 2026, "are on hold" and that the existing terms "remain in effect until further notice". It describes what it shared earlier as "a preview". Meta's address in the terms changes back from 1 Meta Way to 1601 Willow Rd., Menlo Park.

community-feedback-policies-202608.headline: Shows Russian-language footer links, probably an archiving artefact
community-feedback-policies-202608.summary: The archived page shows three footer links in Russian, for the user agreement, the privacy policy and a notice about the EU-US data transfer framework. This looks like an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta, and the policy wording did not change.

community-feedback-policies-202609.headline: Drops the Russian-language footer links seen in the previous copy
community-feedback-policies-202609.summary: The three Russian-language footer links that appeared in the previous archived copy are gone again. They look like an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta, and the policy wording did not change.

community-payment-terms-202412.headline: Moves UK and non-European users to Meta Platforms, Inc. for payments
community-payment-terms-202412.summary: A broad update. Users in the UK and outside the European region now contract with Meta Platforms, Inc. rather than Meta Platforms Ireland Limited for payments other than Meta-Processed Payments, and Meta may get information about users from third parties for tax and compliance purposes. Apple in-app purchasers now let Meta seek refunds from Apple for them, and Meta "will not be held liable" for losses from those refunds.

community-payment-terms-202502.headline: Adds money transmission notices for Arizona, Maine and Minnesota users
community-payment-terms-202502.summary: Meta added a fraud warning for Arizona users, telling them to treat money transmission "like cash; once sent, it cannot be recovered". It also said Meta Payments Inc. is licensed by the Maine Bureau of Financial Institutions, and added a Minnesota Department of Commerce contact for questions or complaints.

community-payment-terms-202507.headline: Adds Service Credits rules, including forfeiture of unused credits for breaches
community-payment-terms-202507.summary: A broad revision. Meta says prepaid "Service Credits" are neither currency nor refundable except where the law requires, and it may keep unused credits if it suspends an account for breaches. Donation refunds now follow PayPal Giving Fund's terms, the EU donation terms and Central Bank of Ireland reference are gone, and free trials and price rises now carry any consent or notice the law requires.

community-payment-terms-202509.headline: Updates Meta's address and adds Arkansas, Connecticut and Vermont notices
community-payment-terms-202509.summary: Meta replaced its old 1601 Willow address in Menlo Park with "1 Meta Way", including for legal notices about payments. It added a fraud warning for Arkansas users and statements that Meta Payments Inc. is licensed as a money transmitter by the Connecticut and Vermont regulators. The last updated date stayed at 18 April 2025.

community-payment-terms-202510.headline: Changes the last updated date to 15 September 2025
community-payment-terms-202510.summary: Only the last updated date changed, from 18 April to 15 September 2025.

community-payment-terms-202602.headline: Adds a Nevada regulator contact for money transmission complaints
community-payment-terms-202602.summary: Meta added a notice telling Nevada users they can contact the Nevada Financial Institutions Division, with a phone number, about questions or complaints on money transmission services. The last updated date moved to 7 January 2026.

community-payment-terms-202605.headline: Adds Payment Partners and new tax reporting and withholding terms
community-payment-terms-202605.summary: Meta added a section on "Payment Partners", such as digital wallets and banks, saying Meta does not process their payments and that using Payment Features means accepting their terms. A tax section makes users responsible for taxes on their transactions unless others collect them, and lets Meta report activity to tax authorities and withhold tax from payouts where the law requires. Meta also added North Dakota and Tennessee regulator contacts.

community-payment-terms-202609.headline: Rewrites payment terms, with creator payout caps and expiring ad credits
community-payment-terms-202609.summary: A broad rewrite of the terms. Meta may now charge other saved payment instruments when one fails, offset chargebacks, fees and fines against amounts owed to users, and "impose or adjust caps on payouts of creators' earnings". Ad credits can expire after three years, or longer if the law requires, currency exchange now covers cryptocurrency, and Meta says it is not liable for third parties' acts, including payment providers.

community-standards-202412.headline: Menu or layout change only
community-standards-202412.summary: Meta added a menu link to a new "Age-Appropriate Content" page about teens on Facebook and Instagram; the Community Standards wording did not change.

community-standards-202502.headline: Lists Hate Speech policy as Hateful Conduct and drops category headings
community-standards-202502.summary: In the list of policies, "Hate Speech" now appears as "Hateful Conduct". The group headings, such as the one for violence and criminal behaviour, are gone, leaving a single list. This page shows only the new name, not any change to the policy's own wording.

community-standards-202503.headline: Menu or layout change only
community-standards-202503.summary: Meta added a menu link to a page called "Tracking the Oversight Board's Impact"; the Community Standards wording did not change.

community-standards-202507.headline: Menu or layout change only
community-standards-202507.summary: Meta added an "Accessibility at Meta" menu link and removed a menu entry on its approach to Facebook Feed ranking; the Community Standards wording did not change.

community-standards-202511.headline: Menu or layout change only
community-standards-202511.summary: The Transparency Center menus are gone from the page and the list of policies is now set out one per line; the Community Standards wording did not change.

community-standards-202606.headline: Shows a differently laid-out copy, not a Meta edit
community-standards-202606.summary: The archived copy runs the value headings (AUTHENTICITY, SAFETY, PRIVACY, DIGNITY) into the text and includes an introduction and a list of policy sections that the copies either side lack. The next copy drops them again, so this is probably a different rendering of the page, not an edit by Meta.

community-standards-202607.headline: Returns to the usual layout after an odd June copy
community-standards-202607.summary: The value headings, the list of policy sections and the line saying the standards apply to "all types of content, including AI-generated content" all appeared only in the June copy and are gone again. The wording matches the May copy, so this is a difference in the archived page, not an edit by Meta.

community-standards-202610.headline: Lists Prohibited Commercial Practices in place of Fraud, Scams, and Deceptive Practices
community-standards-202610.summary: In the list of policies, "Fraud, Scams, and Deceptive Practices" now appears as "Prohibited Commercial Practices". This page shows only the new name, not any change to the policy's own wording.

complaints-handling-process-202602.headline: Replaces separate Facebook and Instagram rule names with Community Standards
complaints-handling-process-202602.summary: The page now says Meta removes content that breaks its terms or policies "including the Community Standards", no longer naming the Facebook Community Standards and Instagram Community Guidelines separately. The updated date moves from 3 September 2024 to 21 March 2025, and a "Transparency Center" menu no longer appears.

developer-payment-terms-202501.headline: Rewords the description of what Facebook Payments does for developers
developer-payment-terms-202501.summary: The opening line now says Facebook Payments lets developers focus on creating apps rather than "content delivery and managing payments", where it used to say "on building payment systems". This is a descriptive edit and no obligations changed.

facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.headline: Loses the reference to US government Pages terms, probably an archiving quirk
facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.summary: The line "Amended Pages Terms for State and Local Governments in the United States" is missing from this copy. It appears in some archived copies of the page and not others, so this is probably an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta.

facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.headline: Restores the reference to US government Pages terms, probably an archiving quirk
facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.summary: The line "Amended Pages Terms for State and Local Governments in the United States" is back after being missing from the previous copy. It appears in some archived copies of the page and not others, so this is probably an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta.

facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.headline: Loses the reference to US government Pages terms, probably an archiving quirk
facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2025.summary: The line "Amended Pages Terms for State and Local Governments in the United States" is missing from this copy. It appears in some archived copies of the page and not others, so this is probably an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta.

facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2026.headline: Restores the reference to US government Pages terms, probably an archiving quirk
facebook-pages-groups-events-policy-2026.summary: The line "Amended Pages Terms for State and Local Governments in the United States" is back after being missing from the previous copy. It appears in some archived copies of the page and not others, so this is probably an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.headline: Drops clickbait and engagement bait from list of content not recommended
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.summary: Meta removed clickbait and engagement bait from its examples of "Content that Users Broadly Tell us they Dislike", one of the categories Facebook may not recommend. Contests and giveaways and links to low-quality landing pages stay on the list.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.headline: Menu or layout change only
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.summary: A related help link changed from "Recommend a business on Facebook" to "How Facebook suggests groups to join", and the guidelines' wording did not change.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.headline: Adds unrelated captions and comment networks to low-quality content
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.summary: Meta added "Long captions unrelated to the underlying content and coordinated comment networks" meant to drive engagement and distribution artificially to its examples of low-quality publishing. Facebook may not recommend content in this category.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.headline: Drops advertising ban as a reason not to recommend accounts
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.summary: Meta removed accounts and entities that "Have been banned from running ads on our platforms" from the list Facebook generally does not recommend. It also retitled the page "About recommendations on Facebook" and changed the related help links.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.headline: Menu or layout change only
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2025.summary: Meta removed the "Was this helpful?" prompt from the page, and the guidelines' wording did not change.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.headline: Menu or layout change only
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.summary: The page heading, feedback buttons and related help links drop out of the page until July 2026, but the guidelines' wording did not change.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.headline: Adds teen age restrictions and drops health, finance and vaccine examples
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.summary: A broad rewrite with a new focus on teens. Meta adds examples of posts it would "age restrict", such as weight loss products and alcohol recipes, and cuts the content it avoids recommending from five categories to three, dropping health and finance claims and contests. Vaccine misinformation is no longer listed, and fact-checking rules now apply only "In countries where Meta supports third-party fact-checking".

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.headline: Drops ties to violent groups as a bar to recommendation
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.summary: Meta removed accounts and entities that "Are associated with offline movements or organizations that are tied to violence" from the list Facebook generally does not recommend. The item is still absent in the September and October 2026 copies.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.headline: Menu or layout change only
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.summary: The page heading, feedback buttons and related help links are missing from this copy and return in October 2026, so this looks like a difference between archived versions rather than an edit by Meta.

facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.headline: Menu or layout change only
facebook-recommendations-guidelines-2026.summary: The page heading, feedback buttons and related help links missing from the September 2026 copy return, so this looks like a difference between archived versions rather than an edit by Meta.

instagram-privacy-policy-202412.headline: Adds account-support selfies to data list, effective 14 November 2024
instagram-privacy-policy-202412.summary: The policy, now effective 14 November 2024, lists a "photo or video selfie" sent for account support among the information Meta uses for purposes such as safety and meeting legal duties. Aggregated analytics reports are now described as helping users as well as businesses, a heading on "AI integrations" appears and Novi drops from the examples of Meta Company Products. A banner announces the update.

instagram-privacy-policy-202502.headline: Removes the banner announcing the November 2024 update
instagram-privacy-policy-202502.summary: Meta took down the notice at the top of the page saying it updated the policy on 14 November 2024, and its link to the previous policy. The policy wording and effective date did not change.

instagram-privacy-policy-202503.headline: Shows a copy without the US regional privacy notice links
instagram-privacy-policy-202503.summary: The archived copy lacks the links to the United States Regional Privacy Notice, which tells US residents how Meta handles their personal information and how to use their privacy rights. The links are back in the next copy, so this is probably a copy of the page served to another region, not an edit by Meta.

instagram-privacy-policy-202504.headline: Restores the US regional privacy notice links
instagram-privacy-policy-202504.summary: The links to the United States Regional Privacy Notice, missing from the March copy, are back, so their absence was probably an archiving difference rather than an edit by Meta. The policy again points US residents to the notice to learn about "the consumer privacy rights that may be available to you".

instagram-privacy-policy-202507.headline: Adds sharing with WhatsApp for linked accounts, effective 16 June 2025
instagram-privacy-policy-202507.summary: The policy, now effective 16 June 2025, says that if users add a WhatsApp account to an "Accounts Center" with other Meta accounts, Meta will link them and "share your information with WhatsApp". It points to a WhatsApp help article for what WhatsApp shares with Meta. Ads are now personalised across "Meta Company Products" rather than "Meta Products", a wider group that includes WhatsApp.

instagram-privacy-policy-202510.headline: Adds a banner announcing AI interactions will personalise ads from December
instagram-privacy-policy-202510.summary: Meta added a banner at the top of the page saying "We'll start using interactions with AIs to personalize experiences and ads", with the change taking effect on 16 December 2025 and a link to the new policy. The policy text itself did not change.

instagram-privacy-policy-202512.headline: Uses AI interactions for ads and to develop AI for third parties
instagram-privacy-policy-202512.summary: In a broad rewrite effective 16 December 2025, Meta lists "Interactions with AI at Meta and related metadata", such as messages exchanged with its AI, among the information used for most purposes, including personalising content and ads. A new purpose lets Meta "Develop and improve AI at Meta for Meta Products and for third parties" using public content and AI interactions. Meta's address changes to 1 Meta Way.

instagram-privacy-policy-202601.headline: Removes the banner announcing the December 2025 update
instagram-privacy-policy-202601.summary: Meta took down the notice at the top of the page saying it updated the policy on 16 December 2025, and its link to the previous policy. The policy wording and effective date did not change.

instagram-privacy-policy-202606.headline: Shows another copy without the US regional privacy notice links
instagram-privacy-policy-202606.summary: As in March 2025, the archived copy lacks the links to the United States Regional Privacy Notice, which tells US residents how Meta handles their personal information and how to use their privacy rights. The links are back in the next copy, so this is probably a copy served to another region, not an edit by Meta.

instagram-privacy-policy-202607.headline: Restores the US regional privacy notice links again
instagram-privacy-policy-202607.summary: The links to the United States Regional Privacy Notice, missing from the June copy, are back, as happened in April 2025. Their absence was probably a copy of the page served to another region rather than an edit by Meta.

instagram-privacy-policy-202608.headline: Covers AI features that "perform actions", effective 23 July 2026
instagram-privacy-policy-202608.summary: The policy, now effective 23 July 2026, says Meta's AI features "do things like create and understand content" and "perform actions", and a banner flags new detail on "agentic AI capabilities". Message metadata joins the information used for several purposes, including personalisation. The link to the US Regional Privacy Notice disappears but returns the next month, so that part is probably an archiving difference.

instagram-privacy-policy-202609.headline: Restores the US privacy notice link, probably an archiving quirk
instagram-privacy-policy-202609.summary: The link to the United States Regional Privacy Notice and the short section for US residents are back after being missing from the previous copy, and they are missing again the month after. This is probably an archiving artefact rather than an edit by Meta.

instagram-privacy-policy-202610.headline: Drops the July 2026 update banner and, again, the US privacy notice
instagram-privacy-policy-202610.summary: Meta took down the banner announcing its 23 July 2026 update on "agentic AI capabilities". The link to the United States Regional Privacy Notice and the short section for US residents are missing again after returning in the previous copy, so that part is probably an archiving artefact. The policy wording and effective date did not change.

instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.headline: Refers to Community Standards instead of Community Guidelines
instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.summary: Two mentions of "Community Guidelines" now say "Community Standards". The recommendation rules around them did not change.

instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.headline: Removes clickbait and engagement bait from content Meta may not recommend
instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.summary: Meta removed one of the five categories of content that is allowed but may not be recommended: content "users broadly tell us they dislike", which listed clickbait, engagement bait and posts promoting a contest or giveaway. Four categories remain, so these kinds of content are no longer named as possibly ineligible for recommendation.

instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.headline: Names Teen Accounts content setting alongside Sensitive Content Control
instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.summary: The note on controlling how much sensitive content people see now also points to "Instagram's Content setting for Teen Accounts", not only the Sensitive Content Control. The rules on what may be recommended did not change.

instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.headline: Rewrites teen rules and drops health and finance category from guidelines
instagram-recommendations-guidelines-202.summary: In a broad rewrite, Meta dropped the health and finance category, so cosmetic procedures, "miracle cures", payday loans and vaccine misinformation are no longer listed, though content promoting weight loss products and cosmetic surgery is now hidden from teens. The teen rules now give examples of what Meta would "age restrict". Fact-checked content is held back only "In countries where Meta supports third-party fact-checking".

instagram-terms-of-use-202412.headline: Drops the promise of at least 30 days' notice before changes
instagram-terms-of-use-202412.summary: The section on updating the terms had two near-identical paragraphs, and Meta removed the one promising notice "at least 30 days before we make changes". The remaining paragraph still says Meta will notify users before making changes, but sets no minimum period.

instagram-terms-of-use-202501.headline: Brings in updated terms on scraping, Meta AI and fact-checking
instagram-terms-of-use-202501.summary: Meta's updated terms, announced for 1 January 2025, replace the old text. The ban on automated access and data collection without permission now applies "regardless of whether" the user is logged in, and a new rule bans getting around technical limits on access. The Meta AI Terms and Avatar Terms now also apply, and Meta says it may add a notice to content rated by fact-checkers.

instagram-terms-of-use-202601.headline: Shows a non-US copy without the arbitration clause, not a Meta edit
instagram-terms-of-use-202601.summary: The archived copy appears to be the version for users outside the US, not an edit by Meta. It has no arbitration clause or class-action waiver, lets consumers sue in their own country's courts, drops the $100 liability cap and sets the minimum age at 13 "or the minimum legal age in your country". The US wording returns the following week.

instagram-terms-of-use-202602.headline: Restores the US terms, with arbitration, after a non-US copy
instagram-terms-of-use-202602.summary: The US version returns a week after a non-US copy was archived, so this is not an edit by Meta. Binding individual arbitration, the class-action waiver, the $100 liability cap and the user's duty to indemnify Meta are all back, and the minimum age is again simply 13.

instagram-terms-of-use-202604.headline: Shows a non-US copy with a minimum age of 14
instagram-terms-of-use-202604.summary: The archived copy appears to be a version for users outside the US, not an edit by Meta. It sets the minimum age at 14, shows an effective date of 1 January 2025, has no arbitration clause or $100 liability cap and lets consumers sue in their own country's courts. The US wording returns in the next copy, in May.

instagram-terms-of-use-202605.headline: Restores US terms, with arbitration and a minimum age of 13
instagram-terms-of-use-202605.summary: The US version returns after a non-US copy archived in April, so this is not an edit by Meta. Binding individual arbitration, the class-action waiver and the $100 liability cap are back, the minimum age returns to 13 and the "Effective Date: 1 January 2025" line goes.

instagram-terms-of-use-202608.headline: Adds Automated Data Collection Terms to the rules on scraping
instagram-terms-of-use-202608.summary: The ban on collecting data in an automated way without permission now covers "Automated Data Collection" as defined in separate Automated Data Collection Terms. Anyone who collects data this way must also follow those terms, and Meta adds that it "may restrict or revoke our permission at any time".

instagram-terms-of-use-202609.headline: Removes the Automated Data Collection Terms references added a month earlier
instagram-terms-of-use-202609.summary: The references to the Automated Data Collection Terms, and the line saying Meta "may restrict or revoke our permission at any time", are gone. The page now matches the July 2026 copy word for word. It is not clear whether Meta withdrew the change or the August copy was a different version of the page.

instagram-terms-of-use-202611.headline: Announces new terms from 20 January 2027; copy may be another region's
instagram-terms-of-use-202611.summary: The November 2026 copy opens with a notice that updated Terms of Use take effect on 20 January 2027. The same copy has no arbitration clause, class action waiver, $100 liability cap or user indemnity, and lets consumers bring claims in their own country's courts. Those are features of the terms Meta shows outside the US, so this copy is probably a different regional version, not a change to the US terms.

music-guidelines-202502.headline: Menu or layout change only
music-guidelines-202502.summary: The guidance on music density, short clips and visual content now appears as separate bullet points rather than one run-on line, and the wording did not change.

music-guidelines-202507.headline: Menu or layout change only
music-guidelines-202507.summary: The guidance on music density, short clips and visual content runs together on one line again, reversing an earlier layout change, and the wording did not change.

partner-monetisation-policies-202605.headline: Shows the full policy text, probably an archiving difference
partner-monetisation-policies-202605.summary: The earlier copy held only Meta for Business menus and a login prompt, so the policy text appearing here is probably a capture difference rather than new rules. The page says creators must live in an eligible country, post original content, have authentic engagement and a 30-day presence, and that politicians, parties and government bodies cannot earn money.

partner-monetisation-policies-202607.headline: Loses the list of monetisation rules, probably an archiving difference
partner-monetisation-policies-202607.summary: The rules on eligible countries, original content, authentic engagement, a 30-day presence and political entities no longer appear, and later copies also lack them. The line "In order to earn money on Facebook, you must:" now leads straight to links, which suggests the rules sit in a part of the page the archive did not capture rather than a removal by Meta.

partner-monetisation-policies-202609.headline: Menu or layout change only
partner-monetisation-policies-202609.summary: A "Have a moment?" heading appears on the page, and the policy wording is unchanged.

partner-monetisation-policies-202610.headline: Menu or layout change only
partner-monetisation-policies-202610.summary: The "Have a moment?" heading under "Learn more" no longer appears, and the policy wording is unchanged.

platform-policy-202502.headline: Rewrites developer terms on data use, incident reporting and enforcement
platform-policy-202502.summary: A broad rewrite, in force from 3 February 2025. A new rule bars processing Platform Data without valid user consent to build or augment user profiles, and the fixed 24-hour deadline for reporting security incidents becomes "as soon as practicable". Meta can now act against apps made to get round its enforcement, and will "use commercially reasonable efforts" to give notice of material amendments.

platform-policy-202508.headline: Adds a supplementary addendum for other international data transfers
platform-policy-202508.summary: Meta added a section, "International Transfer - Other Data Transfers", that brings a Supplementary Data Transfer Addendum into the terms for certain transfers of Platform Data. For those transfers, developers and Meta Platforms, Inc. are each independent "controllers". Meta renumbered the existing EEA and UK transfer sections and moved the last updated date to 22 August 2025.

platform-policy-202511.headline: Announces updated Platform Terms taking effect on 3 February 2026
platform-policy-202511.summary: Meta added a notice saying it is updating the Platform Terms, with the changes in force from 3 February 2026, and a link to "Read the new terms". The wording of the terms themselves did not change.

platform-policy-202602.headline: Adds consent warranty and extends UK transfer rules to developer data
platform-policy-202602.summary: From 3 February 2026, developers who give Meta their content must warrant they hold every consent and disclosure the law requires, and must offer deletion to all users of their app. The UK transfer rules now also cover personal data developers send to Meta, and the description of that data contains bracketed options such as "[TBC]". The Supplementary Data Transfer Addendum becomes the Global Data Transfer Addendum.

political-engagement-policies-202602.headline: Drops pledges on independent expenditures and trade group political spending
political-engagement-policies-202602.summary: Meta removed its statement that it makes no independent expenditures for or against candidates, and its ban on member groups using Meta's payments for political contributions. State giving now aims at "electing candidates who support" certain public policies, not at the policies themselves. Broadly revised lists of member and third-party groups add AI and industry bodies and drop several civil rights and LGBT groups, including GLSEN and The Trevor Project.

political-engagement-policies-202604.headline: Adds two groups to back state candidates and rewrites AI priorities
political-engagement-policies-202604.summary: Meta says it plans to back state candidates "aligned with Meta's policy priorities" through two new Section 527 political organisations. Its lobbying priorities now call for laws requiring app stores to verify age and get parental approval before a child downloads an app. The AI section drops its commitment to open source models and instead cites investment of "hundreds of billions of dollars".

political-engagement-policies-202610.headline: Names four Section 527 groups backing state candidates, up from two
political-engagement-policies-202610.summary: Meta now says it "supports" state candidates aligned with its policy priorities through four Section 527 political organisations, adding "Forge the Future Project" and "Making our Tomorrow" to the two it named earlier. The page adds 2026 contribution and lobbying filing entries, lists infrastructure among its lobbying issues and adds more than 30 state business and technology groups to its memberships.

recommender-system-cards-202502.headline: Menu or layout change only
recommender-system-cards-202502.summary: Meta removed a "Responsibility" link from the AI site menu, and the system cards text did not change.

recommender-system-cards-202505.headline: Menu or layout change only
recommender-system-cards-202505.summary: The AI site menu drops "Product experiences" and adds "Explore Meta AI" and "Get Meta AI" links, and the system cards text did not change.

recommender-system-cards-202607.headline: Menu or layout change only
recommender-system-cards-202607.summary: The AI site menu replaces "Explore Meta AI" and "Get Meta AI" with "Assistant", "Media Generation" and "Vibes", and the system cards text did not change.

recommender-system-cards-202608.headline: Menu or layout change only
recommender-system-cards-202608.summary: Meta reorganised the AI site menu, dropping links such as Llama, Infrastructure, AI Studio and Newsletter and adding AI Research, Learning Hub and Open Source sections, and the system cards text did not change.

recommender-system-cards-202609.headline: Menu or layout change only
recommender-system-cards-202609.summary: The AI site menu adds "Muse", "Agent" and links explaining AI agents and agentic AI, and the system cards text did not change.

self-serve-ad-terms-202502.headline: Menu or layout change only
self-serve-ad-terms-202502.summary: Meta changed the layout of four list items, adding bullet markers and dropping the "Contracting party:" label, without changing the wording of the terms.

self-serve-ad-terms-202506.headline: Adds OCAS Supplemental Ads Terms for EEA online classified ads services
self-serve-ad-terms-202506.summary: Meta added a line saying the OCAS Supplemental Ads Terms apply to advertisers who operate an online classified ads service in the European Economic Area "in line with the European Commission's Decision in Case AT.40684". The effective date moved from 3 January 2023 to 14 February 2025. Other edits restore list labels such as "Contracting party:" without changing the wording.

self-serve-ad-terms-202507.headline: Adds notice that updated terms take effect on 22 August 2025
self-serve-ad-terms-202507.summary: Meta added a notice saying it is updating the Self-Serve Ad Terms, with the changes taking effect on 22 August 2025, and a link to read the new terms. Use of the Self-Serve Ad Interfaces on or after that date will be subject to the updated terms.

self-serve-ad-terms-202509.headline: Rewrites ad terms and lets Meta crawl advertisers' sites for training
self-serve-ad-terms-202509.summary: Meta broadly rewrote the terms, effective 22 August 2025. Placing an Order now lets Meta "access, index, cache, analyze or crawl" advertisers' websites, including for "research and training", and advertisers are "solely responsible" for ad content, targeting and placements. Failing to comply can now mean forfeiting unused Advertiser Balance, and some Orders may be billed through third parties such as Apple, with Meta able to request refunds for them.

self-serve-ad-terms-202610.headline: Adds notice that updated terms take effect on 30 October 2026
self-serve-ad-terms-202610.summary: Meta added a notice saying it is updating the Self-Serve Ad Terms, with the changes taking effect on 30 October 2026, and a link to read them. The wording of the current terms did not change.

self-serve-ad-terms-202611.headline: Puts the planned 30 October 2026 terms update on hold
self-serve-ad-terms-202611.summary: Meta now says the updates to the Self-Serve Ad Terms, which had been due to take effect on 30 October 2026, "are on hold". The notice adds that "The existing Self-Serve Ad Terms remain in effect until further notice", and the "Read the updated Terms" line has gone.

terms-of-service-202501.headline: Brings in Meta's new Terms of Service, effective 1 January 2025
terms-of-service-202501.summary: Meta's new terms replace the July 2022 version and number every section. The bans on automated data collection and on selling Meta data now apply even "while logged-in to a Facebook account", and a new rule bans getting round technical limits on access. The terms also bring in the Meta AI Terms and Avatar Terms and add a note on fact-checkers.

terms-of-service-202511.headline: Shows a non-US version of the terms, probably not an edit
terms-of-service-202511.summary: The archived copy appears to be a version of the terms for users outside the US, not an edit by Meta: it lets consumers sue in "any competent court" in their own country, drops the $100 liability cap and promises 30 days' notice of changes. The US wording returns in the next usable copy, in November 2026.

terms-of-service-202611.headline: Restores the US dispute and liability wording
terms-of-service-202611.summary: The US wording returns after a non-US copy archived in November 2025: disputes again go only to courts in the US under California law, and the $100 cap on Meta's liability is back. The only new wording is minor: a comma, and "that content" in place of "this content" in the licence clause.
